soundness_flags.label: def:feasible-score; thm:feasible-score-expansion; thm:uniform-wald-coverage
soundness_flags.one_line: The advertised observable criterion invokes derivative and covariant-Hessian norms defined only for the truth-indexed experiment Theta_q(P), g_q, and K_q, but gives no fitted experiment or formula that maps (tilde M_a, Chat_aq) to the required charts and norms; hence Crit_n and qhat are not fully specified measurable maps.

soundness_flags.label: def:adaptation-frontier versus def:guarded-predecessor-covariance and thm:feasible-score-expansion
soundness_flags.one_line: Delta_P infimizes over every 0<=q_N<N and 0<=q_T<T, whereas the implemented selector searches only q_N<=floor(b_N/4), q_T<=floor(b_T/4); no assumption or theorem relates that restricted candidate set to the unrestricted frontier used on the right-hand side.

soundness_flags.label: thm:legal-lower-experiment
soundness_flags.one_line: The theorem and lower-product construction require a 'relative-interior sequence' and epsilon_leg(P,q)>0, but neither the ambient tail-class topology nor the relative-interior condition ensuring a positive legal radius is defined.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: ass:oracle-regularity / thm:uniform-wald-coverage
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The uniform comparison c0 sigma||W_n||_F <= s_P(W_n) <= C0 sigma||W_n||_F is maintained, not derived, over the full Ferrers class.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Uniform Wald coverage is claimed conditional on ass:oracle-regularity; the balanced L-mask calculations are stated only as verification for their named target families.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper uses double-sample debiasing and singular-space projection for linear forms under its noisy matrix-completion experiment; its asymptotic variance depends on alignment with U and V.
The paper studies a low-rank counterfactual panel with general intervention pattern Z and gives rate-optimal recovery for its average treatment effect.
The paper gives no-sample-splitting low-rank-completion inference; the auxiliary leave-one-out estimator is a proof device, while the implemented procedure uses the full observed sample.
GEMINI estimates row and column covariance/inverse-covariance graphical structure from a single matrix-normal realization under sparsity conditions.
The paper proves deterministic lower-bound tightness and matching minimax risks for low-rank-plus-sparse matrix recovery with arbitrary entrywise noise dependence.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define a fitted finite-sieve experiment explicitly: specify the estimated horizontal quotient, covariance-factor coordinates, Riesz map, and exact formulas for every quantity entering d_hat_q and h_hat_q, including guard/fallback behavior.
Make the oracle and feasible frontiers use the same bandwidth domain, or add a primitive tail-exponent/design condition proving an oracle band pair has a constant-factor representative in Q_n.
Replace the undefined relative-interior clause by explicit strict slack conditions for every class constraint and prove a quantitative positive lower bound for epsilon_leg(P,q).

Add a formal common-subclass variance calculation showing that each named Choi--Yuan and Choi--Kwon--Liao statistic is standardized by the same s_L(h), rather than only asserting a shared N(0,1) limit.

recommended_next_step: Revise the feasible selector and lower-experiment definitions to make their claimed frontier comparison well-posed, then resubmit this field-tier novelty angle.
